A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same kernel-regression account of in-context learning. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and publication layout.

before.justification: V2 reports original GPT-J attention analyses, feature probes, prediction-reconstruction results, and downstream evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical analyses and adds input-perturbation results, synthetic-HMM experiments, Llama analyses, and a single-example visualization.

M1.justification: The HMM-derived kernel, weighted-label reconstruction, attention-weight extraction, and ridge probes remain substantively unchanged. The additional models and synthetic experiments evaluate the existing proposal; head selection concerns evaluation.

E1.justification: The six original language-classification tasks remain. V3 adds a synthetic-HMM domain in Appendix C and distinct SST2 test conditions involving rare-word substitutions, complex sentence structures, and typos in Section 4.2.

E2.justification: GPT-J ICL, all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and bert-base-nli-mean-tokens remain in the downstream comparison. V2's separate overall-best-head KR comparison disappears; v3 reports one selected-head reconstruction and performance pair.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 revises the reported head-selection procedure from best reconstruction accuracy to highest correlation with model predictions. Added experiments introduce GPT-3.5-turbo input transformations, a synthetic-HMM sweep over 1–128 demonstrations, and Llama-2/Llama-3 8B evaluations. V3 also explicitly documents selection and held-out evaluation sets, without establishing whether that separation was absent in v2.

E4.justification: V3 adds tests of sensitivity to input perturbations, synthetic convergence with demonstration count, generalization of attention/reconstruction patterns across models, and a single-example attention case study. These appear in Section 4.2 and Appendices C–E; the existing Appendix B analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The plotted averages over examples or heads and the theoretical probability bounds do not constitute new empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V3 replaces the best-head result summaries: for example, v2's task-specific SST2 reconstruction accuracy is 0.864 and MNLI KR task accuracy is 0.974, whereas v3 reports 0.797 and 0.360 under its revised selection description. These are replacement results, not established same-setting performance decreases. New results include SST2 accuracy of 0.805, 0.677, 0.788, and 0.534 for clean, rare-word, complex, and typo inputs, plus synthetic and additional-model findings. The GPT-J and sentence-encoder baseline scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix A change the stated remainder from little-o to big-O at the same n^(-1/2) scale. The posterior derivation also incorporates full-prompt conditioning and test-input likelihood factors in v3 Equations 31–34. These are limited formal revisions within the retained theorem and proof framework.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the kernel-regression hypothesis, the asymptotic Bayesian-inference connection, the attention/hidden-feature agreement claim, and the three practical ICL insights. V3's perspective-oriented wording does not materially change this central claim set.

C2.justification: V3 expands the distribution-mismatch discussion into arguments about pretraining bias and departures from Bayesian behavior, adds substantive HMM expressiveness and efficiency limitations in Section 7, and clarifies possible implementation across multiple layers. Section 5.5 also replaces v2's interpretation of KR sometimes outperforming ICL with a model-level performance interpretation. The sample-ordering limitation already existed in v2.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project code/resource URL and documents the perturbation generator and synthetic-HMM dimensions: 8 tasks, 80 states, and 100 observations. It newly specifies 700 validation examples for head selection and 300 held-out examples per task; v2 does not provide corresponding counts. These disclosures do not establish that previously undocumented settings changed.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 substantially expand positioning around non-Bayesian ICL, optimization algorithms, training dynamics, algorithm selection, and associative memory. Added discussions include Falck, Raventós, Park, Fu, Bai, and other works, broadening the comparison beyond v2's emphasis on Bayesian inference and constructive gradient-descent accounts.

P1.justification: The main narrative sequence and much existing prose remain. V3 updates the title and front matter, removes the introduction's contribution bullets, revises related-work and evaluation passages, and adds a limitations section and appendices. The existing document undergoes localized rewriting rather than wholesale reorganization.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a substantially different publication layout, resizes and relocates figures, adds explicit axis labels to Figures 3 and 5, and consolidates the reconstruction/task summaries into one table. It also adds the perturbation and synthetic tables and Figures 21–25. Appendix B's underlying plots are retained despite their changed placement and sizing.

improvement.justification: V2's empirical support centers on GPT-J and indirect attention/probe agreement. V3 adds synthetic verification, perturbation and cross-model checks, explicitly documents held-out evaluation, and states important HMM/Bayesian limitations. Together these substantially strengthen and qualify the evidence for the central hypothesis. Removing the overall-best-head comparison loses some cross-task evidence, and empirical uncertainty remains unreported, but those limits do not outweigh the gains.
